Original current_ref (libyasummit.com, dead) recovered as a Wayback capture (2024-06-14) of the same live article: confirms Libya is 'spearheading several new pipeline projects – including the 130-km NC 41-Mellitah Gas project to commence from 2025 and owned by Eni and the NOC.' Independently, Offshore Technology/GlobalData's dedicated NC 41-Mellitah Gas pipeline profile describes it as 'upcoming' and 'expected to commence operations in 2025.' Neither source prints the literal word 'construction', but both independently confirm the pipeline as a named, owned, dated (2025), committed infrastructure project actively being developed rather than merely proposed/conceptual — status inferred as construction per standard practice (a reasonable reader concludes construction-stage from a dated, owned, in-development project). CAVEAT TO FLAG: I found no source (English/Arabic/Italian) independently confirming an actual construction/pipe-laying milestone specifically for this 130km/30in NC-41-Mellitah segment (as distinct from the offshore Structures A&E development or the Sabratha compression project, which are separately documented and have their own pipelines). Confirmed this source is genuinely about THIS line (30in, 130km, Bay of Tripoli to Nuqat Al-Khams) and not the separate P6715 E Structure-Mellitah line (36in, ~30km, Structure E to existing Sabratha-Mellitah pipeline) or the unrelated 42in Intisar A/103-to-Brega pipeline (also 130km, trialled April 2026 per Ecofin/PGJ) that surfaced in searches and is a different project entirely.

No ambiguity.

PipelineType=transmission is a GEM taxonomy classification (transmission vs. gathering vs. distribution), not a term sources use verbatim. Offshore Technology's profile describes a 130km, 30in-diameter trunk line carrying gas between two named points (Bay of Tripoli area and Nuqat Al-Khams/Mellitah) — a long-haul line-haul pipeline is the standard basis for a 'transmission' classification, as opposed to a short field-gathering line. Only one source gives the specific route/diameter needed to support this classification directly (the libyasummit.com piece confirms the project exists and its length/date but not diameter/route), so staged at medium/single-source per the confidence-tier convention rather than left blank.

Status=construction reconfirmed by 3 independent, live, verified sources, all specifically about the Structure E / Structures A&E development (not the sibling P6708 NC 41-Mellitah Gas Pipeline, which is a distinct line out of the same NC-41/Contract Area D concession -- checked route/segment descriptions in each source to keep them separated). (1) offshore-technology.com project page: describes the Structure E gas export pipeline design and states first gas/onstream 'expected...in 2026' -- i.e. not yet operating. (2) attaqa.net (Al-Taqa, Arabic energy trade outlet, 2025-08-11): reports Mellitah Oil & Gas (NOC/Eni JV) signing an $8bn EPC-related contract package (with Hill International as project management consultant) with commercial startup still targeted for 2026 ('بدء التشغيل التجاري المتوقع في عام 2026'), confirming the project is still being built, not operating. (3) petrogaslibya.com 2026 outlook piece: still describes Structures A&E as scheduled to start production in 2026, i.e. under construction. No source found reporting FID reversal, cancellation, or an early/actual startup. The sheet's prior current_ref combo (mellitahog.ly/.../02.pdf + offshore-technology.com?cf-view) both actually resolve live once the tracking query string/redirect wrapper is stripped -- the mellitahog.ly PDF (see Length/Diameter units) is a real 2021 Mellitah Oil & Gas prequalification tender document, but it's a project-scope document from a pre-construction planning stage, not a current-status source, so I did not reuse it here; the more recent independent sources above are better evidence for current Status.

Automated screen reports this URL as 'value not found' -- that is a false negative: the check reads the raw HTTP body, which for a PDF is a compressed binary stream, not searchable text. Downloaded the PDF and ran pdftotext manually: it IS live (HTTP 200, 6-page PDF) and is Mellitah Oil & Gas B.V.'s own Feb-2021 EPCIC prequalification tender ('A&E STRUCTURES, MELLITAH COMPLEX EXPANSION & CO2 MANAGEMENT INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT PROJECT'). It explicitly and separately describes the Structure A route (18in/43km to Sabratha Platform -- a different segment, not this one) and the Structure E route: 'A new gas sealine (32" to be verified during FEED) 130 km long [deliver] E Structure production to Mellitah' -- 130 km matches the sheet's recorded LengthKnown exactly. IMPORTANT CAVEAT (per brief): this is the pre-FEED design estimate. The project's later, post-FID (2023) public description at offshore-technology.com instead states a shorter, revised design -- 'A 30km-long and 36in-diameter gas pipeline will deliver production from Structure E to an existing 36in gas export pipeline from the Sabratha Platform to the Mellitah Complex' -- i.e., after FEED, Structure E ties into the EXISTING Sabratha-Mellitah trunk rather than running a new 130km line all the way to Mellitah as originally scoped. So the sheet's 130km value is real and sourced (matches this primary document exactly) but reflects an earlier design phase; the apparently 'final'/most-recent figure per offshore-technology.com is 30km. Only ONE source gives 130km specifically for the Structure E sealine (a similar, earlier 2018 mellitahog.ly scope-of-work doc gives the same ~130km distance but a 30in diameter -- same operator, not independent, so not counted as a second source). Flagging this design-stage discrepancy for the data team; staged as medium/single-source rather than fabricating a second independent confirmation of 130km specifically.

Same source and same caveat as the Length unit above (see that entry for full detail on the manual PDF verification). The same sentence in Mellitah Oil & Gas's Feb-2021 EPCIC prequalification tender gives diameter explicitly: 'A new gas sealine (32" to be verified during FEED) 130 km long [deliver] E Structure production to Mellitah' -- 32in matches the sheet's recorded Diameter exactly, with the document's own caveat that this figure was still 'to be verified during FEED' at the time. Per the brief's caution: the project's later, post-FID (2023) design at offshore-technology.com instead specifies 36in for the Structure E export tie-in ('A 30km-long and 36in-diameter gas pipeline will deliver production from Structure E to an existing 36in gas export pipeline from the Sabratha Platform to the Mellitah Complex'), and a related condensate line is separately given as 14in (2021 doc) vs 10in (2023 source) -- consistent evidence the design was revised between the 2021 pre-FEED tender and the 2023 post-FID public description. Only one source (the 2021 tender) supports 32in specifically; no second independent source found giving 32in (the 2018 scope doc gives 30in instead, and is not independent of the 2021 doc -- same operator). Staged as medium/single-source; flagging the 32in-vs-36in discrepancy for the data team rather than silently reconciling it.

Status=construction supported (inferred, not literal token). Libya Herald (2026-05-07, translating a 5 May NOC/Mellitah statement) reports the Bouri Gas Utilisation Project (BGUP, DP3/DP4/Sabratha platforms) at '69% complete, exceeding the planned percentage,' with a cargo ship of project units then en route to the field to 'begin heavy lifting and technical linkage to platforms (3) and (4)' — i.e. not yet in service. Oil & Gas Journal (2026-06-29, on the separate but adjacent Sabratha Compression Project startup) states in the same piece that 'Bouri gas utilization project, whose tie-in and commissioning activities are currently underway after the recent installation of the Bouri gas recovery module' — confirming BGUP (this pipeline's parent project) is still under construction/commissioning as of late June 2026, not yet operating. Two independent outlets (Libyan business press; US trade journal, Endeavor Business Media — unaffiliated with Eni/NOC/Saipem), both dated 2026, both confirming ongoing (not completed) construction. NOTE: excluded the Saipem 2023-08-09 press release from this unit despite being on-topic, since Saipem discloses the BGUP award as a 'related party transaction' (Eni jointly controls both Saipem and Mellitah Oil & Gas) — not independent of the owner.

Flagging for Baird: recommend checking whether the mainsheet StartYear1 should actually read 2026 given the weight of current evidence, or whether 2028 reflects an internal estimate/source not surfaced by this search.

Two independent sources, both explicitly distinguishing the 8/8.5km DP3-DP4 line from the 20km DP4/Bouri-Sabratha line.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Libya and EndLocation='Sabratha platform' supported. NS Energy Business: 'The Bouri Field is located offshore in Block NC-41, about 120km northwest of Tripoli in the waters of Libya' and describes the DP3/DP4 line feeding into the DP4-to-Sabratah pipeline ('the DP3 and DP4 platforms will be connected...to transport the raw gas from DP3 to DP4' immediately followed by the 20km line 'to Sabratah Platform'), i.e. the DP3-DP4 segment is upstream of, and part of the same offshore Libyan system terminating at, the Sabratha platform. Libya Herald corroborates: pipelines 'to connect the two platforms [DP3/DP4], and another...line to connect the Al-Bouri field to the Sabratha platform and from there to the Mellitah Industrial Complex on the north western Libyan coast' — confirms Libya as the country for the whole interconnected DP3/DP4/Sabratha system and Sabratha platform as the terminal endpoint referenced by the GEM row's EndLocation field. Two independent sources.

(2) libyaherald.com (Libya Herald, bylined Sami Zaptia, editor-in-chief) — independently reports the same Sept 2024 meeting and the agreement to prepare an MoU on feasibility studies for a Nigeria-to-Europe pipeline via Libya; does not cite the 5,600km figure itself but corroborates the proposal/talks. (3) libyareview.com (Libya Review) — separate Libyan outlet, confirms the Nigeria-Libya pipeline discussion (via Niger/Chad to Europe) though its 5,600km reference is to the competing Nigeria-Morocco/NIGAL route, not this one; cited for corroboration of the talks themselves, not the distance figure. (4) ecofinagency.com (Ecofin Agency, pan-African financial/trade press, bylined Abdel-Latif Boureima) — a later, distinct story (Sept 2025) reporting 'revived' Nigeria-Libya pipeline talks, feasibility studies, and a planned MoU, citing a somewhat different route length (~3,300km) than the brief's 5,600km — treated as corroborating the underlying proposal/talks (status = proposed), not the specific distance. Status 'proposed' is confirmed by inference across all four: feasibility studies, technical exchanges, and a planned-but-unsigned MoU, with no construction or FID reported anywhere. Sources span three outlets/countries (Nigeria, Libya x2, pan-African wire) and two distinct reporting cycles (2024, 2025) — genuinely independent, not the same wire story republished.

Status=construction (DP4-Sabratha segment, part of the Bouri Gas Utilisation Project / BGUP) confirmed by inference across four independent outlets, none of which use the literal word 'construction' but all describe the project as mid-build, pre-commissioning: Offshore Magazine (ABL overseeing installation of platform modules, ongoing EPCIC scope of laying the 28 km DP3/DP4-Sabratha pipeline network); Offshore Engineer/oedigital (May 2026: fabrication 69% complete vs 62% planned, modules just shipped from Ravenna, platform tie-in and pipeline pre-commissioning still ahead); NOC Libya's own release (same 69%-vs-62% milestone, gas units installed on DP4 but production not yet started); and attaqa.net (Arabic, 2025-07-10: pipelines/platforms description with the project described as due to start operating 'next year' i.e. 2026, not yet in service). All are consistent with construction/pre-commissioning, not operating.
